basics.name: Jeff Randow
basics.label: Healthcare IT Developer · Security · Instructional Associate
basics.summary: Healthcare IT developer and security practitioner with 13+ years running the data, integrations and endpoint security behind a 16-clinic nephrology practice that serves about 30,000 patients a year. Also an Instructional Associate at Georgia Tech, supporting a networking course that averages 1,200 students per semester. M.S. in Computer Science; B.S. in Environmental Engineering.

work.name: San Antonio Kidney
work.position: Healthcare IT Developer and Security Administrator
work.note: Embedded with Panoramic Health, the practice's managed-services provider, until September 2026. Returned to practice employee status October 2026.
highlights: Designed and maintain a daily export pipeline (Python, Pandas, Transact-SQL, XLSXWriter) that moves thousands of clinical, billing, claims, financial and admin rows a day from the Veradigm EHR/PM system into the managed-services data warehouse. In production about 8 years and updated through every major EHR/PM upgrade.
Built and support about 7 bi-directional HL7 interfaces between labs, providers and the EHR, including the XML transforms needed to import results into the chart.

Built a Flask clinical portal used by about 40 internal staff to manage patients on a hemoglobin-raising drug. It combines EHR and PM data, charts history, shows lab levels and insurance eligibility, and warns when lab data is stale.
Automated clinical, accounting and billing reports into a self-service portal, giving about 40 staff on-demand data and replacing manual report requests (SSRS, SSMS, Transact-SQL).
Develop against the Veradigm Unity API and FHIR to integrate and extract EHR data, and design internal APIs for the practice's tools.

Run endpoint and identity security for 95 users across 16 clinics (11 full-time, 5 part-time), covering EDR/XDR, endpoint protection, Azure remote access and identity protection, with 20 physicians and 5 nurse practitioners relying on it.

work.name: Georgia Institute of Technology (OMSCS)
highlights: Help teach CS 6250 Computer Networks and CS 8200 Graduate Introduction to Operating Systems in the online M.S. in Computer Science. The networking course averages about 1,200 students per semester.

Own the SDN Firewall project end to end, including grading and academic-integrity follow-up. Migrated it from the Pyretic to the POX OpenFlow controller and updated it for Python and controller changes.
Maintain and support the Mininet-based Simulating Networks project.
Run chat sessions and office hours to support students.
